source.title: Learning Dynamics of Deep Matrix Factorization Beyond the Edge of Stability
source.authors: Avrajit Ghosh; S. Kwon; Rongrong Wang; S. Ravishankar; Qing Qu

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present, including appendices.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports its own results on learning dynamics beyond the stability threshold in deep linear matrix factorization and selected nonlinear networks, a setting distinct from the listed benchmark classification claim.
record.gate_note: The reported results concern oscillations, sharpness, balancing and loss behavior; they do not report training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100. The CIFAR-10 sharpness plot varies dataset subset size, but supplies no recoverable numerical results in the text.
record.test_reason: The study directly tests V5's edge-of-stability dynamics through its own loss and Hessian-sharpness results in deep linear matrix factorization and nonlinear networks. Classification error is unnecessary for testing V5. It distinguishes sustained oscillations from recovery to a flatter basin and tests when progressive sharpening reaches the stability threshold.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's conclusion is broadly accurate. The authors characterize two-period subspace oscillations and balancing toward the flattest minima in deep matrix factorization, alongside a period-doubling route to chaos. Their nonlinear experiments illustrate mild sharpening and oscillations in leading features. The theory concerns limiting behavior near balanced minima under singular-vector stationarity, rather than complete training dynamics.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes full-batch gradient descent on deep linear matrix factorization with squared Frobenius loss, plus selected nonlinear-network examples; the claim versions center on classification error, shortcuts, initialization, learning-rate recovery and batch normalization.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior varies with learning rate and target singular-value scale; the CIFAR-10 sharpness behavior varies with the number of training examples. The paper also reports that balancing may fail at initialization scale α = 0.5 while singular-value oscillations remain.

fits_no_version.finding: Sustained singular-value oscillations reduce cross-layer imbalance toward zero under suitable initialization and learning rates.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent beyond the stability threshold can balance deep linear matrix factors through sustained oscillations.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss oscillations in four-layer ReLU MLPs on MNIST and CIFAR-10 are concentrated in top singular-value directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Oscillatory training dynamics in some nonlinear networks concentrate in leading feature directions.

record.problems: The core theoretical and experimental analysis concerns deep linear matrix factorization, not benchmark classification error. The nonlinear-network observations are largely figure-based and qualitative; no classification training-error values are reported. The authors note that their analysis focuses on behavior around balanced minima and assumes singular-vector stationarity for the main analysis.

untested.parts: Near-zero training classification error in sufficiently large convolutional networks, including random-label experiments and recipe-dependent exceptions.
Spurious-minimum frequency in ReLU teacher-student networks and its reduction through extra student neurons.
Depth-dependent training-error degradation and prevention through identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Activation-matched initialization effects on learning speed and trainable depth, orthogonal-versus-Gaussian speed comparisons, and extremely deep convolutional training.

Recovery specifically relative to the initial linearized wide-network stability limit; a systematic comparison of recovery and divergence learning rates; and divergence despite initially subthreshold learning rates. R2–R3 do not establish continuing loss reduction or sustained threshold hovering.
Batch-normalization comparisons of training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and Fixup comparisons.

missing.what: Joint training-loss and sharpness trajectories showing progressive sharpening followed by threshold hovering and periodic loss oscillations in depth-3 matrix factorization.
The learning-rate-dependent existence of sustained two-period orbits beyond the balanced-minimum stability threshold, distinguishing bounded oscillation from convergence.
Mild sharpening versus entry into EOS when a fixed-initialization UNet fits low-frequency versus higher-frequency target images; SGD with η = 0.0002.

record.verdict_notes: This study is not an original source for the listed versions. V5 explicitly includes sharpness dynamics, so the absence of classification-error measurements does not exclude its EOS results. The relevant stability threshold in the matrix-factorization theory is determined at balanced minima, rather than by the initial linearized model. No numerical values were inferred from unavailable figure images.

versions.untested_parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100, random or corrupted labels, model size, optimizer comparisons, early stopping and regularization.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima frequency and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual shortcut comparison for training error, depth comparisons on ImageNet/CIFAR-10, and normalization-free residual training.
Activation-matched initialization comparisons for plain networks, orthogonal versus Gaussian initialization, and 10,000-layer convolutional training.

The study tests beyond-threshold behavior in deep linear networks and reports loss/sharpness oscillations, but its squared-loss deep matrix factorization setup does not match V5's wide-network recovery claim or its sharpness trajectory measures as framed. A nonlinear MLP's loss oscillations are shown only in a figure.
Batch normalization speed and learning-rate tolerance comparisons, and Fixup residual training without normalization.

rows.subject: 3-layer end-to-end DLN
rows.size_stated: Each layer Wℓ ∈ R50×50; target matrix M⋆ ∈ R50×50 with rank 3 and singular values 10, 9.5, 9
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent on deep matrix factorization loss; learning rate selected for rank-1 oscillation
rows.measure: Balancing gap across layer singular values over iterations
rows.value: Balancing gap decays monotonically to zero as long as the learning rate is chosen such that periodic oscillations occur in the top-3 subspaces
rows.note: The text describes the plotted result but gives no numeric gap values.
rows.check: Balancing-gap decay is observed, but it does not itself measure V5's loss recovery or sharpness trajectory. The operation detail incorrectly says rank-1 oscillation: Figure 7(left) uses η > 2/S3, producing oscillations in all three target subspaces.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: 2 layers; trained on N labeled training images from CIFAR-10; N values discussed include 100, 200 and above 1000
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MSE loss; sharpness tracked during training
rows.value: For small N values, such as 100 or 200, the network learns only a limited set of latent features, resulting in mild sharpening, and it does not reach the EOS threshold
rows.note: This is a sharpness result, not training classification error; the text does not give numerical values.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports failure to reach the EOS threshold for N = 100 or 200. This measures the progressive-sharpening component of V5, rather than classification error. The extracted numbers_found value is spurious; full-batch optimization is not specified for this experiment in the supplied description.

source_check.correct: state: partial. Sharpness increases mildly but remains below the EOS threshold for N = 100 or 200.
source_check.locator_found: Section 4.2, mild-sharpening paragraph; Figure 10(c) and caption.
source_check.problem: Mild sharpening is an incomplete effect, so partial fits the state rules better than absent.

rows.subject: 2-layer fully connected neural network
rows.size_stated: 2 layers; trained on N labeled training images from CIFAR-10; N exceeds 1000
rows.operation_detail: Trained with MSE loss; sharpness tracked during training
rows.value: When N exceeds 1000, the sharpness increases and reaches the EOS threshold
rows.note: This is a sharpness result, not training classification error; the text does not give numerical values.
rows.check: The text explicitly reports sharpness increasing to the EOS threshold for N > 1000. This establishes threshold approach, but the row does not establish subsequent hovering or continuing loss reduction. The extracted numbers_found value is spurious.

rows.subject: 3-layer MLP without bias terms
rows.size_stated: Each hidden layer consists of 1000 units; trained on a 5K subset of MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Full-batch gradient descent with MSE loss and random weights scaled by α = 0.01
rows.measure: Training loss, top-5 singular values and sharpness over iterations
rows.value: Oscillations appear to be almost periodic across all three plots
rows.note: The text states the qualitative finding; no values are recoverable. This does not measure classification error.
rows.check: Loss and sharpness are relevant measures, but almost-periodic oscillations alone do not establish their position relative to 2/η or long-timescale loss reduction. The qualitative observation is stated in Appendix B.4, so evidence_form should not be exclusively figure_only.

rows.subject: 4-layer MLP with ReLU activations
rows.size_stated: Hidden layer size 200 in each unit; classification on a subsampled 20K set
rows.operation_detail: Training dynamics evaluated for oscillations in training loss and top singular values
rows.measure: Training loss oscillations associated with top singular values
rows.value: The oscillations in the training loss are artifacts of jumps only in the top singular values
rows.note: The statement does not quantify classification training error.
rows.check: Concentration of loss oscillations in top singular-value directions does not establish above-threshold recovery or EOS sharpness dynamics. The qualitative result is explicitly stated in Appendix B.4.
